conventions.convention: A scalar model has m>0, a nondegenerate open time interval I₀, a nonempty open configuration interval Q, and a continuous force F:I₀×Q×R→R locally Lipschitz in (x,v), locally uniformly in time. Motions are C² curves on intervals with nonempty interior; included endpoints use domain-relative derivatives.

The conservative presentation is F=−U′ with a declared time-independent C² potential U and zero residual force. Mechanical energy is mv²/2+U(x); adding a constant changes its numerical level but not the force.

Phase distances use dimensionless numerical SI coordinates x=Xphys/(1 m), v=Vphys/(1 m/s), with Euclidean norm sqrt(x²+v²). A turning position of energy E₀ means U(x)=E₀; it need not be a simple turning position.
The harmonic model has I₀=Q=R, k>0, F=−kx and U=kx²/2. Its nonzero-amplitude maximal motions have least period 2π/ω; zero amplitude gives the rest motion, with every time shift a period.
Linear damping permits c≥0; strict damping means c>0. The declared force is −kx−cv, and the potential representative remains kx²/2. At c=0 this is the harmonic model.

The prescribed sinusoidal drive has real amplitude f₀ and strictly positive angular frequency Ω. Its source has no modeled back-reaction. The physical model excludes Ω=0, although the mathematical amplitude supplier permits a continuous extension there.

The pendulum example adopts an angular chart equation with dimensionless θ, generalized inertia ml² and torque −mgl sin θ. It is expressly outside the translational scalar model class; its finite-time bound uses normalized time and phase coordinates.
Strict-minimum stability concerns the unrestricted autonomous equation on R×Q×R, even if the declared physical time window I₀ is smaller; this does not enlarge the declared model window.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the scalar model data, standing continuity and state-Lipschitz regularity, C² motions satisfying mx″=F(t,x,x′), phase field (v,F/m), potential presentation F=−U′+d, energy, equilibria and oscillator-type data (m,c,k,f).

For the declared conservative scalar model with C² potential U, every datum has exactly one maximal motion; energy mv²/2+U is constant along every motion; U(x(t))≤E₀, velocity is ±sqrt(2(E₀−U(x(t)))/m) when U<E₀, and x′=0 exactly when U=E₀; rest motions correspond exactly to U′=0.

Harmonic motions are A cos(ω(t−t₀))+B sin(ω(t−t₀)), with ω=sqrt(k/m), A=x₀ and B=v₀/ω. Their maximal extensions have domain R, amplitude R=sqrt(A²+B²), energy kR²/2, least positive period 2π/ω when R>0, and phase image equal to the displayed ellipse; R=0 gives the rest point.

For m>0, k>0 and c≥0, motions are classified into two-exponential, critical (A+Bt)e^(−ct/(2m)), and damped sinusoidal families according to c²−4mk. Every datum has one maximal motion on R. Energy satisfies e′=−c(x′)² and the corresponding integral identity; for c>0 constant energy is equivalent to the zero rest motion.

For m>0, k>0 and c>0, the stated casewise position and velocity bounds hold for t≥0; dimensionless constants depending only on normalized model parameters bound both coordinates by the initial phase norm. Every maximal motion tends to zero together with its velocity, and the origin is globally asymptotically stable.

For the declared sinusoidal drive with Ω>0, the displayed particular response solves the equation, every maximal motion exists on R and differs from it by a homogeneous motion. Strictly damped motions are bounded forward and their position and velocity transients vanish; undamped off-resonant motions are bounded on R; nonzero undamped resonant drive makes every maximal motion unbounded forward. The amplitude maximum has the stated c²<2mk, c²≥2mk and f₀=0 cases.

A strict local minimum of the C² potential gives a Lyapunov stable rest point of the unrestricted autonomous phase equation. Its derivative linearization is mξ″+U″(x*)ξ=0; only when U″(x*)>0 is this the harmonic model with frequency sqrt(U″(x*)/m).

concerns.concern: Statement clause 1 displays families in unshifted t, then says 'its coefficients are the ones supplied by clause 4 ... for the shifted curve s↦x(t₀+s)'. Those are coefficients in s, generally different from the displayed coefficients in t. For m=k=1, c=0, datum (π/2,1,0), the shifted coefficients are A=1,B=0, whereas the unshifted motion is sin t, with A=0,B=1. The statement needs to distinguish the two coefficient systems or explicitly shift the displayed families.

Fact L3 says 'the coefficients A,B carry length'. In the critical family (A+Bt)e^(λt), A has length dimension but B=v₀−λx₀ has velocity dimension. At the declared critical datum B=1 m/s, not 1 m. This dimensional assertion is false even though the numerical critical solution is correct.

Verification 3.1 says that in the underdamped case energy strictly decreases 'at every time except t=2πn/√3, n≥0'. The motions were declared globally on R, and x′ also vanishes at negative integer multiples; for example t=−2π/√3 gives e′=0. A forward-time restriction is missing from this sentence, or the exceptional index must range over all integers.

Clause 4 asserts that a specified ellipse point is attained at 'exactly the times' displayed. Proof 3.2 establishes attainment at those times but does not explicitly establish the converse. The missing immediate argument is that equal cosine and sine pairs imply their angle difference has cosine 1 and sine 0, hence belongs to 2πZ by the cited zero-set and shift identities.

Fact L6 says that for a≥0, y²=a has 'exactly the two solutions y=±sqrt a'. At a=0 there is one distinct solution. The proof uses the two-distinct-values assertion only for a>0 and handles zero separately, so this is a wording defect in the auxiliary fact.

alerts.finding: The Proof technique paragraph says 'convert the monotonicity through the strictly decreasing maps x↦1/x and x↦sqrt x'. The square-root map is strictly increasing on its nonnegative domain, as Fact F3 and proof 3.1 correctly state. The erroneous introductory description should be corrected; the actual monotonicity proof uses the right direction.

seams_checked.note: The scope remark uses the pendulum supplier only with its finite-time, smallness and no-exact-harmonicity qualifications; the worked specialization is on the companion page.
The scalar potential presentation, residual forces and declared potential representative preserve the supplier's distinctions. Conservation is proved locally for time-independent U.
Standing force regularity, phase reduction and maximal-motion language are preserved. The scalar class is explicitly adopted rather than deduced from the three-dimensional branch.
Fixed positive mass and SI dimensions are preserved; phase norms explicitly normalize unlike physical dimensions before adding coordinate squares.
Stability uses maximal solutions and forward existence, rather than arbitrary local restrictions. The strict-minimum theorem explicitly specifies the unrestricted autonomous extension.

Classification, decay, response and amplitude-maximum hypotheses otherwise match. The damped-motion statement conflates the supplier's coefficients at zero for a shifted curve with its own displayed unshifted families; see the assigned-item concern.
Strict-minimum stability and derivative linearization use the n=1 constant-positive-metric specialization with C² U. Harmonic identification additionally requires U″(x*)>0.
Most SI and normalized-coordinate uses agree. The damping example's L3 incorrectly assigns length to the critical coefficient B; the units supplier requires velocity dimension there.

The examples use classification at t₀=0, positive damping for decay, nonzero drive for resonant unboundedness, and f₀≠0,c²<2mk for the positive-frequency amplitude maximum. Numerical evaluations match the exact expressions.
The pendulum specialization has ω²=L=||A||=1, δ=1/100, r=1/2, T=1 and δe<r. Its error majorant is te^(3t)/(12·10⁴), with no claim beyond the stated horizon.
The angular pendulum uses the constant metric ml² and C² potential −mgl cos θ, expressly outside the translational scalar class. Stability and linearization retain the mathematical chart hypotheses.

The scalar harmonic identification requires positive stiffness; zero stiffness is treated separately. Weak damping uses c=εγ>0. Prescribed sinusoidal forcing respects Ω>0, with Ω=0 supplied separately by the general continuous-force model.

The forced-mode example preserves prescribed-drive status and separates positive-frequency sinusoidal forcing from constant forcing. The averaging example adopts the strictly damped model with c=10⁻⁴ kg/s.
The harmonic Hamilton–Jacobi, caustic and critical-fibre examples preserve m,k>0, the quadratic potential and harmonic motion family. Period assertions expressly exclude the constant motion.

The stability-without-attraction counterexample uses the m=k=1 harmonic family at datum (δ,0), δ>0, and its nonzero period to exhibit failure of convergence; it makes no damping or empirical assertion.
